prompt: A cereal filling machine produces boxes whose weights are normally distributed with mean $16.1$ oz and standard deviation $0.3$ oz. A random sample of $9$ boxes is weighed. What is the probability that the sample mean is less than $16.0$ oz? Use $P(Z < -0.33) = 0.3707$, $P(Z < -1) = 0.1587$, $P(Z < -3) = 0.0013$. Round to four decimal places.
hint: The question is about a sample mean of $9$ boxes, so standardize with the standard deviation of $\bar{x}$, which is smaller than $0.3$.

hints.text: The question is about a sample mean of $9$ boxes, so standardize with the standard deviation of $\bar{x}$, which is smaller than $0.3$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: if $\sigma = 2$ and $n = 4$, then $\sigma_{\bar{x}} = 2/\sqrt{4} = 1$. Here do the same with $0.3$ and $9$.
$\sigma_{\bar{x}} = 0.3/\sqrt{9} = 0.1$. Compute $z = \frac{16.0 - 16.1}{0.1}$ and pick the table value that matches it.
$z = -1$, so the probability that the sample mean is below $16.0$ oz is $P(Z < -1) = 0.1587$.

explanation: Because the population is normal, $\bar{x}$ is normal for any $n$, with mean $16.1$ and standard deviation $0.3/\sqrt{9} = 0.1$ oz.
Standardizing $16.0$ with that standard deviation gives $z = \frac{16.0 - 16.1}{0.1} = -1$.
$P(Z < -1) = 0.1587$, so there is about a $16\%$ chance the 9-box average comes in under 16 oz.

alternativeExplanations.title: Spot the decoys
steps: Using $\sigma = 0.3$ (one box) gives $z = -0.33$ and $0.3707$ — that answers a different question: ONE box under 16 oz.
Dividing by $n = 9$ instead of $\sqrt{9}$ gives SD $0.033$, $z = -3$ and $0.0013$ — too small.
The sample mean uses $\sigma/\sqrt{n} = 0.1$, giving $z = -1$ and $0.1587$.
